intro.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to find the maximum depth of a binary tree, which is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. The core programming concept used is recursion, where the function calls itself to traverse the tree's left and right subtrees. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, conditional statements, and tree node objects. You'll learn how to handle base cases for empty trees and recursively compute depth. By the end, you'll understand how to apply recursion to solve tree-based lessons efficiently.
intro.usecase: Finding the maximum depth of a binary tree is essential for optimizing data structures in real-world applications like file systems and UI component trees. For example, in a content management system, a nested folder hierarchy can be represented as a binary tree, and calculating its maximum depth helps determine the deepest level of subfolders for efficient navigation and storage management. Similarly, in a React application, the component tree's depth impacts rendering performance, and understanding tree depth aids in debugging and optimizing re-renders. This algorithm is also used in game development for AI decision trees, where evaluating the deepest possible move sequence is crucial for strategic planning.

objectives: Construct a recursive function to traverse a binary tree structure.
Implement a base case to handle empty (null) nodes during tree traversal.
Apply a depth-first search approach to calculate the maximum depth from each subtree.
Integrate the Math.max function to compare and select the greater depth from left and right child nodes.
Initialize a binary tree node structure with value, left, and right properties for testing.
Manipulate the traversal logic to return the correct integer depth count starting from 1 at the root.
Configure a test case by building a sample binary tree and invoking the maximum depth function.

content.body: How deep can a tree go? In this lesson, we'll find the maximum depth of a binary tree. You'll learn to explore branches systematically and measure how far down they reach.
content.title: Introduction

content.body:
• Explain what maximum depth means for a binary tree
• Apply depth-first search to explore tree branches
• Implement a recursive function to calculate maximum depth
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: Look at this simple tree with root value 3, left child 9, and right child 20. How many levels does it have? Count from the root down to the farthest leaf.
content.title: Explore a small tree
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: Now consider a tree with root 1, left child 2 (which has left child 4), and right child 3. What's the maximum depth now? Follow each branch to its end.
content.title: Try a deeper tree
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: What if the tree has no nodes at all? What should the maximum depth be? Think about what happens when we try to explore branches from nothing.
content.title: What about an empty tree?
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body: You manually traced each branch from the root to its end, counting levels as you went. This works for small trees but would be tedious for large ones.
content.title: What you did

content.body: Real trees can have hundreds of nodes with complex branching. We need a systematic way to explore all branches without getting lost or missing any.
content.title: Why we need a method

content.body: Trees are explored by following branches from the root. At each node, we can go left, go right, or if we've reached the end (a leaf), we stop. The maximum depth is the longest path we find.
content.title: Tree exploration thinking
content.visualMetaphor: Use branch/root visual reasoning; visiting nodes or exploring levels one at a time.

content.body: We can use recursion: the depth of a tree is 1 (for the current node) plus the maximum depth of its left and right subtrees. For an empty tree, depth is 0.
content.title: The recursive approach
content.visualMetaphor: Show exploring from the root down branches; one level or one branch at a time.

content.body:
1. If the tree is empty, return 0
2. Otherwise, calculate depth of left subtree
3. Calculate depth of right subtree
4. Return 1 + the larger of the two depths
